notes: The editor timeline now shows the yellow start and end handles in full when a clip reaches the start or end of the video, so you can see and drag them. The clip length and the Title tab at the top are no longer cut off.

New clips now start unticked for export, so only the ones you choose are exported and sent to ContentPilot. You can tick a clip with the new Export checkbox next to its title in the editor; ticked clips show ✓ in the editor's clip list.

Trimming a clip in the editor is now frame-accurate: while you drag a yellow edge you see the exact frame it lands on, and holding Option moves it slowly, frame by frame, without snapping to words or sentences. The ← → keys now step one frame (⇧← ⇧→ one second).

Fixed: after making a Reel from the video editor with "One Reel with the whole edit", every new video came out as a single full-length clip instead of short clips. That Reel no longer changes what you chose for other videos.

Copy and paste sound in the video editor: select an audio clip or a piece and press Cmd+C (mark I and O first to copy only part of it), then Cmd+V pastes it at the playhead — on another audio track if something already plays there.
You can now stop a voice/background separation in progress with the Cancel button next to its progress bar; the edit stays as it was.

High-quality voice separation: an optional one-time install (Demucs, about 1 GB, runs on your Mac) separates voices from music much more cleanly — voices no longer leak into the Background track. A piece you already separated can be separated again to replace its tracks.

New in the video editor: a Mute track button at the left of each track (video and every audio row) mutes or unmutes the whole track in one click — for example, mute Background after separating voice and background.

New in the video editor: Separate voice and background. Right-click a piece or an audio clip to split its sound into two tracks — the voice alone and the music/noise — so you can lower, remove or replace either one. Everything is processed on your Mac.
Right-click a video in an edit's Media panel (or in the links list) and choose Show in Finder to open the folder where it is saved. Links can also be copied from the right-click menu.
The update window is now always in English.
First version with automatic updates (Sparkle). New identifier com.trinitycommerce.clipmaker; your preferences carry over automatically.
